# Conclusion

K-means clustering can effectively separate northern Chilean bofedales into meaningful groups with distinctive characteristics that can inform on the ecosystems’ health.

- With our data, various metrics indicated k=11, which yields well-separated clusters
- Clusters indicate unhealthy/outlier bofedales (such as cluster 7)
- The algorithm was able to incorporate a diverse array of environmental factors
- Factors such as protected land or mining sites can inform policy decisions relating to water management or conservation
